titulo: Security gate closed + per-tier position sizing + tighter CEX stop-loss
motivo: Self-analysis of 13 closed positions (3 wins, 10 losses): dex_micro_cap lost a net -€57.85 across 6 closes (16.7% win rate) versus +€6.49 net from cex_small_cap across 7 closes (28.6% win rate) — almost the entire challenge deficit was concentrated in a single tier. TRUMPSTACY bought at score 90 even without a confirmed GoPlus check and rugged -99.5%; the 5 real stop-losses in cex_small_cap always closed between -11.8% and -18.4% instead of the configured -10%.
mudanca: scoring.py: a dex_micro_cap candidate without a confirmed security check (checked=False) is now eliminated, not just penalized. config.py: STOP_LOSS_PCT[cex_small_cap] from -10% to -8%. config.py/portfolio.py: new POSITION_SIZE_PCT_BY_TIER — dex_micro_cap from 25% to 12% of equity per position, cex_small_cap stays at 25%.
efeito_esperado: Fewer buys of dex tokens without a real security check; stop-loss losses in cex_small_cap closer to -10%; and when a dex_micro_cap position still collapses, the impact on the total balance is half of what it would have been before.

titulo: Capital circuit breaker (halts new entries at -75% drawdown)
motivo: Ricardo asked directly what would happen if the challenge balance reached zero. In a strategy with no leverage/margin the balance never goes negative, but until now nothing stopped fresh capital from continuing to be risked on new entries during a severe losing streak.
mudanca: config.py: new MAX_DRAWDOWN_HALT_PCT = -75% (halts when equity <= 25% of the starting balance, €25 of €100). portfolio.py: _check_entries() now checks the threshold every run — once hit, marks capital_protection_active=True, sends a one-time Telegram alert (_alert_capital_protection), and stops opening NEW positions; already-open positions keep being monitored and closed normally (take-profit/stop-loss/trailing/forced liquidation at the end of the 10 days). telegram_alert.py: the portfolio status message now indicates when protection is active.
efeito_esperado: If the challenge enters a very severe losing streak, the remaining capital stays protected in cash instead of staying exposed to new entries — it's a permanent circuit breaker for the rest of the challenge, not an auto-reset (it won't start opening positions again just because equity recovered a bit).

titulo: Fixed a bug that restarted the challenge without any decision (git race + silent reset)
motivo: 2026-08-31: screener.yml (every 2h) and bot_listener.yml (every 15 min) both write to data/portfolio_state.json; a "git pull --rebase --autostash" conflict between the two runs left conflict markers ("<<<<<<< Updated upstream" etc.) committed into the file instead of resolved. load_portfolio() treated any read failure as "no state" and silently returned a default state (€100, no positions) — this restarted the 10-day challenge on its own, without any decision by me or a request from Ricardo, losing the closed-position history from the state file (lessons.json and wins.json were corrupted the same way, but kept most of their history visible in Git).
mudanca: (1) screener.yml and bot_listener.yml now share the same concurrency group (crypto-screener-git-state) so they can never run at the same time — the root cause of the git conflict. (2) The git step in both workflows now detects a "git pull --rebase" failure and aborts without committing, instead of blindly continuing. (3) portfolio.load_portfolio() now raises PortfolioStateCorrupted instead of returning a default state when the file exists but isn't valid JSON; main.py, position_monitor.py, and the Telegram /status command catch this exception, alert on Telegram, and abort the run WITHOUT writing anything over the corrupted file (to allow manual recovery from Git history).
efeito_esperado: The challenge should never again restart on its own due to file corruption — a run with unreadable state now aborts and alerts on Telegram instead of masking the problem. Since the new cycle (ZORA/HEMI/HOOKR/ZKC, from 2026-08-31) already had real trades (HOOKR and ZKC sold), I decided to keep this new cycle as the current challenge instead of trying to reconstruct the previous one, but the full pre-incident history remains recoverable from Git history if Ricardo prefers to revert.

titulo: Selection no longer blindly prefers the most "stretched" candidate above score 90
motivo: End-of-challenge self-analysis (79 closed trades, 2nd 10-day cycle, 2026-09-10): the correlation between entry_score and pnl_pct was -0.019 (practically zero) — the score did not predict the outcome. The 90-100 bracket (46 of 79 trades, 58%) was the WORST bracket in net € of all of them (-€36.22), and the average entry_score of the losses (90.4) was HIGHER than that of the wins (82.0) — in other words, within what already passes the filters, the most extreme candidate (the one that rose the most, the fastest) was not the better pick; it tends to already be stretched near the top of the move (e.g., PERPSPAD bought twice at score ~99, fell both times). This confirms the measured problem is in candidate selection, not in stop-loss/take-profit sizing (which remain unchanged). Limitation identified: only the final combined score was being stored per trade, not the raw signals that compose it — so it's not yet possible to isolate WHICH specific signal (chg_1h, chg_24h, turnover, ...) is at fault, only that the combined score as a whole has no predictive power.
mudanca: portfolio._check_entries(): when choosing among several eligible candidates at once, no longer always breaks ties by the highest raw score — above config.SELECTION_SCORE_CEILING (90), the score is now treated as tied and the tiebreak becomes liquidity (most liquid first). Also, the raw entry signals (entry_chg_1h, entry_chg_24h, entry_chg_7d, entry_chg_6h, entry_turnover, entry_vol_liq_ratio, entry_boosted) are now stored on every closed position/trade (portfolio.py) and in the lessons/wins (lessons.py, playbook.py), so a future self-analysis can break results down by signal.
efeito_esperado: Reduce the likelihood of systematically buying the most stretched candidate (which this cycle's data shows is, if anything, a worse choice) when equally qualified alternatives exist; and, above all, gather enough data (raw signals per trade) for the next self-analysis to actually isolate which score component does (or doesn't) have predictive power, instead of repeating this same high-level conclusion again in 10 days.

titulo: "Stable base followed by breakout" signal (dex_micro_cap) + persistent trailing stop
motivo: Ricardo brought 4 real DEX tokens (EMBER, CME, UP, BNC4) the bot never alerted on. In 3 of them (EMBER, CME, UP) the price had a relatively calm phase before a strong breakout — a pattern the scoring at the time didn't distinguish from a pump that IS the token's own birth (the 4th example, BNC4, rises almost vertically in its very first candles and dies right after). Separately, the old `_watch_trailing_stop` only watched a blocking 5-minute window after the first take-profit touch and closed the position unconditionally at the end of that window, even mid-rally — a local simulation (entry 1.0 -> peak 21.0 over several runs) confirms this would have sold near the start of the move instead of near the top.
mudanca: scoring.py: new detect_base_breakout() function — uses the already-collected chg_6h and chg_24h (no extra API calls) to approximate the implied price move in the ~18h before the breakout window; gives a score bonus (new weight DEX_WEIGHTS['base_breakout']=0.25, at the expense of reducing chg_1h 0.35->0.25, chg_6h 0.20->0.15, vol_liq_ratio 0.30->0.25) only when there's a calm base (config.DEX_BREAKOUT_MAX_PRE_WINDOW_MOVE_PCT=25%) and the pool already has credible history (config.DEX_BREAKOUT_MIN_POOL_AGE_HOURS=24h). portfolio.py: removed the blocking _watch_trailing_stop (time.sleep); the peak is now persisted on the position itself (trailing_active/trailing_peak_eur) and re-evaluated on every run (screener every 2h, the light monitor every few minutes), with no fixed deadline — it only closes on a real pullback (TRAILING_STOP_DRAWDOWN_PCT=7%) from the highest peak seen so far. Also started storing entry_pool_age_minutes and entry_base_breakout in every position's snapshot (previously missing), so a future self-analysis can validate this signal with real data instead of manual examples.
efeito_esperado: More genuinely-breaking-out DEX candidates (not just birth pumps) should now reach ENTRY_MIN_SCORE; this is NOT expected, by itself, to distinguish winners (like UP) from reversals (like EMBER/CME) — that part remains the job of the exit-side stop-loss/trailing stop. The persistent trailing stop should capture a larger fraction of sustained rallies than the old mechanism (which only watched a fixed 5 min), at the cost of reacting to a reversal only on the next run instead of immediately (a 'gap' risk between checks, inherent to how often position_monitor.py runs).

titulo: Entry liquidity tiebreak now actually works for the CEX tier (volume_24h proxy)
motivo: Investigating the LSK position (+256.9% at the peak, fell back to a 399M MC) showed that SELECTION_SCORE_CEILING (see the 2026-09-10 change) breaks ties between candidates above the ceiling by liquidity_usd — but sources_coingecko.py never populates that field for cex_small_cap candidates, only DEX candidates have real liquidity. Since almost all challenge positions are cex_small_cap, the tiebreak was inert exactly where it mattered most.
mudanca: screener/portfolio.py: new _robustness_proxy() function used in _check_entries()'s sort — keeps liquidity_usd when it exists (DEX) and uses volume_24h as a robustness/liquidity proxy when liquidity_usd is None (CEX). Also fixed an outdated test in tests/test_portfolio_offline.py (Run 2b, written for the old blocking trailing stop) and added a new test (Run 2c-ter) covering the tiebreak with CEX-tier-shaped real data.
efeito_esperado: The robustness/liquidity tiebreak above the score-90 ceiling now has a real effect on most entries (CEX tier), reducing the blind preference for the most stretched candidate when several pass the threshold at once.

titulo: New experimental 'Pump Watch' system — accumulation signal, independent of the main challenge
motivo: Ricardo's request from 2026-09-14: the main challenge only buys what's already rising (momentum). Asked to test a different signal — accumulation/distribution that typically precedes a swing move (days to weeks) — to see if it helps anticipate pumps before the price reacts.
mudanca: New module screener/pump_watch.py: an accumulation signal via normalized OBV (On-Balance Volume) over CoinGecko's hourly history (screener/sources_coingecko.fetch_market_chart, new), computed only for a small shortlist (PUMP_WATCH_SHORTLIST_SIZE=10) to conserve the shared API quota. Fully independent from the main challenge: its own virtual balance ($100, PUMP_WATCH_STARTING_BALANCE_EUR), up to 3 concurrent positions, only enters when a slot is free, exit is ALWAYS a pure 10% trailing stop from the peak (no fixed take-profit), with 20% of each realized PROFIT reserved (never reinvested) and the rest + the capital returned to tradable cash — losses don't get this cut. Covers only the cex_small_cap tier for now (CoinGecko, more reliable data; GeckoTerminal/DEX left for a future iteration). No fixed deadline (unlike the main 10-day challenge) — it's a continuous signal test — but with a review checkpoint at 10 closed trades or 20 days (whichever comes first), for a self-analysis to evaluate the results. Wired into main.py (full 2h cycle) and position_monitor.py (exit check every few minutes, runs even when the main challenge is inactive). Its own Telegram messages (telegram_alert.format_pump_watch_message) and a new /pump bot command. Tested with 8 offline scenarios (tests/test_pump_watch_offline.py): signal math, entry+shortlist, trailing stop from entry and after a rise, profit reserve, loss without the cut, full slots (no wasted API call), and corrupted state.
efeito_esperado: Allow comparing, over weeks, whether an early-accumulation signal (buying before the price reacts) has a better hit rate/return than the main challenge's pure momentum — without risking contaminating either system's results.

titulo: Weak-position rotation: frees a slot when an already-qualified new candidate has nowhere to enter
motivo: Direct request from Ricardo (2026-09-16): he noticed that strong signals in the discovery alert (Crypto Screener — new momentum signals) never made it into the Virtual Portfolio Challenge, and asked whether it would be better to sell a weak position to make room for a stronger one. Diagnosis: with MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS=4 slots all occupied, _check_entries returned immediately (before evaluating anything), ignoring already-qualified candidates until an existing position closed on its own — made worse by the bot_listener.yml bug (fixed in this same session) that had left all exits frozen for more than 24h, likely keeping the slots full during exactly the period Ricardo observed.
mudanca: New screener/portfolio._maybe_rotate_weak_position function, called from _check_entries only when slots_free <= 0 and there's at least one eligible candidate waiting. Deliberately does NOT compare the new candidate's score to the closing position's score — the 2026-09-10 self-analysis already showed raw score doesn't predict return (correlation -0.019 across 79 closed trades, and the 90-100 bracket was the WORST in net €), so a higher score is not, by itself, a valid reason to sell an open position. Instead, it applies the same decay signal the bot already trusts (SCORE_DECAY_EXIT) EARLIER, with three guardrails: (1) position score below ROTATION_SCORE_WATCH=45 (between neutral and the 30 exit threshold) and no unrealized gain at all; (2) position open for at least ROTATION_MIN_HOLD_HOURS=4; (3) a global cooldown of ROTATION_MIN_INTERVAL_HOURS=12 between rotations, to avoid churn. New constants in config.py (ROTATION_ENABLED/ROTATION_SCORE_WATCH/ROTATION_MIN_HOLD_HOURS/ROTATION_MIN_INTERVAL_HOURS). Test coverage: Run 8 (rotation happens correctly with all 4 slots full) and Run 8b (the three guardrails block rotation when they shouldn't fire) in tests/test_portfolio_offline.py — the full suite (including the pre-existing Runs 1-7b) validated locally before pushing, zero regressions.
efeito_esperado: Already-qualified new candidates (score >= ENTRY_MIN_SCORE) are no longer systematically ignored just because the 4 slots are occupied — but only when the weakest position already shows real signs that its thesis has faded (this is not a speculative swap for "whoever rose more"). Should reduce how often the pattern Ricardo reported happens (good discovery signals that never enter the challenge) without reintroducing the already-detected problem of picking by raw score.

titulo: Reduced position size in cex_small_cap (real stop-loss ~2x worse than the trigger)
motivo: Self-analysis of 54 closed trades (37 real cex_small_cap stop-losses since the -8% trigger introduced on 2026-08-30): the real average loss on those 37 closes was -15.32%, almost double the trigger, with missed_updates=0 in EVERY case (not a data-gap issue). 12/37 (32%) closed worse than -15%, including AIN at -80.08% (alone, at 25% position size, it cost ~20% of total equity) and several between -20% and -29% (OTC -29.3%, LOOM -27.6%, PERPSPAD -26.3%, POWER -23.5%, CVC -20.6%). Even excluding the AIN outlier the average is -13.52%, still ~70% worse than the trigger. No strong correlation with entry liquidity/volume (CVC and REZ had >$150-190M in 24h volume and still overshot the trigger by >10 points) nor with holding time (correlation of 0.07 between hours-to-close and pnl_pct) — this points to discrete price jumps larger than the ~15-minute gap between position_monitor checks can catch near the trigger, and tightening the trigger from -10% to -8% on 2026-08-30 had already failed to improve the real average.
mudanca: config.py: POSITION_SIZE_PCT_BY_TIER["cex_small_cap"] from 0.25 to 0.15 (25% -> 15% of equity per position) — the same logic already applied to dex_micro_cap on 2026-08-30 (scaling position size down by the measured loss overshoot: 0.08/0.1352 ≈ 0.59 -> 25%*0.59 ≈ 15%), since the problem isn't solvable by tightening the stop-loss further or with an obvious entry filter. No change to exit logic (stop-loss/take-profit/trailing stay the same) — only to bet size.
efeito_esperado: Shouldn't change the expected return per position (gains and losses scale by the same 0.6 factor), but reduces the tail risk of any single cex_small_cap position — an AIN-type collapse now costs ~12% of equity instead of ~20%, further from the -75% circuit breaker (MAX_DRAWDOWN_HALT_PCT). A future self-analysis should compare the pnl_eur distribution (not just pnl_pct) of cex_small_cap positions closed before/after this change.

titulo: Fixed repeat data corruption from git autostash race + recovered frozen portfolio
motivo: On 2026-09-20 13:58 UTC a 'git pull --rebase --autostash' conflict between bot_listener.yml and screener.yml (same failure mode as the 2026-08-31 incident, despite the shared concurrency group added back then) left literal Git conflict markers committed inside data/portfolio_state.json, data/lessons.json and data/pump_watch_state.json (commit c696554), making them invalid JSON. The existing safety net (load_portfolio() raising PortfolioStateCorrupted instead of silently resetting the challenge) worked as designed: it aborted every run without touching history, but that meant it also fired a Telegram alert on every single run since then (~every 5 min via bot_listener.yml) for about 18.5 hours, and the virtual portfolio was completely frozen (0 opens/closes) the whole time, while the unrelated alerting part of screener.main kept working normally (data/state.json kept updating). Comparing the conflicting sides confirmed the local run's changes were a stale duplicate of closes already present in the previous valid commit (1b2fd2c) — no real trade history was at risk, just the merge itself.
mudanca: (1) Restored data/portfolio_state.json, data/lessons.json and data/pump_watch_state.json to their last known-good state (commit 1b2fd2c), verified byte-for-byte after publish. (2) Hardened the 'Guardar estado' step in both screener.yml and bot_listener.yml: after 'git pull --rebase --autostash', explicitly check for unmerged files (git diff --diff-filter=U) and leftover conflict markers; if found, discard this run's local recompute in favor of the already-published remote state (git checkout --ours) instead of ever committing conflict markers again. The run simply skips saving this cycle; the next one (minutes later) recomputes from the now-correct base.
efeito_esperado: No more risk of conflict markers being committed to the JSON state files when this autostash race recurs (it clearly can, a second time, even with the concurrency group in place) — worst case is one skipped save cycle instead of a multi-hour frozen challenge plus dozens of duplicate Telegram alerts. Portfolio tracking (69 closed trades so far) resumes normally from this point.

titulo: Challenge #1 ended (-22.4%) — archived, challenge #2 started with 1000 EUR
motivo: Balanço da challenge #1 (10-20 set, 10 dias): 100€ → 77,58€ (-22,42%), 73 trades fechados, 24,7% win rate. Maior ganho: LSK +310% (trailing stop apanhou uma subida de +385% desde a entrada). Maior perda: AIN -80,1% (stop-loss, colapso quase total).
mudanca: Challenge #1 encerrada e arquivada (data/challenge_history.json); challenge #2 arrancou com saldo de 1000€ (subido de 100€, a pedido do Ricardo).
efeito_esperado: Challenge #2 usa exatamente a mesma estratégia já testada e ajustada ao longo da #1, agora com 10x mais capital simulado.
